han that Aprille
with his his shoures soote /
The drouȝte of Marche hath perced to the roote
And bathed eueri veyne in such licoure
Of wich vertu engendred is the floure
Whan zephirus eke with his soote breth
Enspired of eueri holte and heth
The tendre croppis and the yong sonne
Hath in the Ram his half cours I ronne
And smale foules make melodie
That slepen all niȝt with open yhe
So prikketh hem nature in her corages
Than longen̄ folk to gon on̄ pilgrimages
And Palm
ur
es to seke straung strondes
To serue halwes couthe in eueri londes
And specialli from eueri shires ende
Of Engelond to Caunterbury thei wende
The holi blisfull martir for to seke
That hem hath holpen whan þ
ᵗ
at
thei were seke
Befel in that season vpon̄ a day
In Southwerk at the Tabard as I lay
Redi to wende on my pilgrimage
To Caunterbury with deuoute corage
At niȝt was come in to that hostelrie
Well xxix vpon̄ a companie
Of so
n
dri folk be auenture I falle
In felaship and pilgrymes were thei alle
That toward Caunterbury wold ride
The hambres and stables were wide
And were wel easid ate beste
And shortli whan the sonne was to reste
So had spoken with hem euerichon̄
That I was in her felaship̄ anon
And made forward erli for to rise
To take oure weie there as I you deuise
But neuertheles whiles I haue space
Er that I forther in to this tale pace
Me thinketh it is  accordant with reson
To telle you alle the condicio
ıı̄
un
Of eueri of hem̄ so as semeth me
And wich they were . and of what degre
And eke in what array they were inne
And at the kniȝt than woll I beginne
A
kniȝt ther was
and
that aworthi man̄
That fro the tyme that he first began̄
To rid
t he loued chiualrie
Trouthe honour fredam and curtesie
Full worthi was he in his lordes werres
And therto had he riden noman so ferre
As wel in cristendam as in hethenesse
And euer honoured for his worthinesse
At Alisaunder he was whan it was wonne
Fuloftyme he had the boord begonne
Aboue all nacions in Pruce
In Lectowe had he riden and in Ruce
No cristen man so often in his degre
In Garnade at the siege there had he be
Of Algazire and riden in Belmarie
At Lyes was he and at Satalye
Whan they were wonne
and
in the grekissh see
At many anoble Ryuer had he be
At mortall batailles had he ben fiftene
And fouȝten for oure feith at Tramisshene
In lystes thries  and alwey slain his foo
This ilke worthi kniȝt had ben also
Somtime with the lord of Palacie
Ayenst an othir hethen in Turkye
And euermore he had souerein pris
And thouȝt that he was worthi and wise
And of his port as meke as a maide
Ne neuer yit no vilenie seide
In all his lif to no maner wiȝt
He was verri gentill and parfiȝt kniȝt
For to telle you of his array
His horse were goode but he was nat gay
Of fustian he war a gipo
ıı̄
un
All be smotreid with his habergeo
ıı̄
un
For he was late I come from his viage
And wente for to don̄ his pilgrimage
U
ith him ther ws his Sone a yong Sqire
A louer and a lusti bacheler
With lockes crulled as they wereleid in presse
Of twenti yere of age he was I gesse
Of his stature he was of euene lengthe
And wonder delyuer and of gret strengthe
And he had somtyme ben in chiualrie
In Flaundres in Artrois and in Picardie
And born him well as in litill space
In hope to stonde in his Ladyes grace
Embrouded was he as it were a mede
All full of fressh floures white and rede
Synging he was and florting al the day
He was as fressh as is the month of May
Short was his goune his sleues long
and
wide
Wel coude he sitte an hors and faire ride
And coude songes make and wel endite
Iouste and daunce wel portraye and write
So hoot he loued that be niȝter tale
He slepte nomore than doth a Niting hale
Curteis he was louli and seruisable
And kerue beforn his fader at the table
A
yoman he had and seruauntes nomo
As at that tyme for him list ride so
And clad he was in cote and hood of grene
A shef of Pecok arwes briȝt and shene
Vnder his belte he s bar full thriftily
Wel coude he dresse his takill yomanly
His arwes drouped nat with fetheres lowe
And in his hand he bar a miȝti bowe
A notted hed had he with a broun visage
Of woodcraft coude he all the vsage
Vpon̄ his arme he bar a gay bracer
And on that othir side a gay dagger
And be his side a swerd and a bokeler
Harneised well
and
sharpe as point of spere
A cristofre on his breest of siluer shene
An horn he bar the baudrik was of grene
A fostere was he sotheli as I gesse
T
her was also a Nonne a Prioresse
That of her smiling was ful simple
and
coy
Her grettest othe was be Seint Loy
And she was callid madame Eglentyne
Full well she sang the seruice diuine
Entuned in her nose full semely
And frenssh she spak full wel
and
fetisly
Aftir the scole of Stratford of the bowe
For frenssh of Parys was to hir vnknowe
At mete well tauȝt she was with all
She lete no morsell from hir lippes fall
And wett her fyngers in her sauce depe
Wel couthe she carie a morsell and kepe
That no droppe fell on her brest
In curtesie was sette full mochel her lest
Hir ouir lippe wiped she so clene
That in her cuppe no ferthing was ther sene
Of grece whan she had dronke hir drauȝt
Full semeli aftir hir mete she rauȝt
And sikirlich she was of gret disport
And full plesaunt and full amiable of port
And peined hir to counterfete chere
Of court and to ben estatli of manere
And to be holde digne of reuerence
But for to speke of hir conscience
She was so charitable and so pitous
She wolde wepe yef she saw a mous
Caught in a trappe if it were ded or bledde
Of smale houndes had she that she fedde
Of rosted flessh or milk or wastell bred
But sore she wepte yef oon of hem were ded
And if men smot hem with a rodde smerte
All this was conscience of a tender herte
Full semeli hir wimpill pinched was
Hir nose thrilles hir yhen greye as glas
Hir mouth full small and therto softe
and
red
But sekirli she had a faire forhed
It was almost a span brod I trowe
For hardli she was nat vndergrowe
Full fetise was hir cloke as I was war
Of small corall aboute hir arme she bar
A peire of bedes the gaudees al of grene
And theron henge a broche of gold ful shene
On wich ther was writen first a crouned A
And aftirward Amor vincit omnia .
An othir Nonne with hir had she
That was hir Chapelein and prestes three
A
Monke ther was a faire for the mastrie
An outerider that loued wel venery
A man̄ to ben an Abbott able
Full many a deinte hors had he in stable
And whan he rod men miȝt his bridell hiere
Gyngling in a whistling wynde as clere
And eke as loude as a chapell belle
Ther as this lord was keper of his selle
The rule of seint Maure or of seint Benet
Be cause it was holden somdell streite
This ilke Monke lete olde thinges passe
And holde after the newe world the space
He yaf nat of the text a pulled henne
That seith hunters beth nouȝt holi men̄
Ne that a monk whan that he is recckeles
Is lik a fissh that is waterles
This is to sey a monk withouten̄ his cloistre
But that text halt he nat worth an oistre
And I said his opinion was good
What shuld he studnd make him selue wood
Vpon̄ a book alwey in cloistre and poure
Or swinke with his handes in laboure
And Austyn hou shall the world be serued
Late Austyn haue his labour to him reserued
Therfore he was a pricasour a right
Greyhoundes he had as swifte as foul of fliȝt
Of Priking and of hunting for the hare
Was al his lust for no cost wold he spare
I sauȝ his sleues purfiled at the hand
With grys and that the fynest of the londe
And for to fasten the hood vnder the chyn̄
He had of gold wrouȝt a full curious pyn̄
A loue in the gretter ende ther was
His hed was balled and shon as glas
And eke his face as it had ben enoynte
He was a lord full fat and in good point
His yhen stepe and rolling in his hed
That stemed as a forneis of a Led
His bootes souple his hors in gret estat
Now certainli he was a faire prelat
He was nat pale as a for pined gost
A fat swan loued he best of any roste
His Palfrey was as broun as any berie
A
frere ther was a wanto
ıı̄
un
and
a merie
A lymitour a full solempne man̄
In all the ordres foure ther is non þ
ᵗ
at
can
So mochell of daliaunce and faire language
He had made many a faire mariage
Of yong wommen̄ of his ougne coste
Vnto his ordre he was a noble poste
Full welbeloued and familier was he
With frankeleines oueral in his contre
And eke with worthi men of eueri toun̄
For he had power of confessio
ıı̄
un
As he seid him self more than the curatt
For of his ordre he was licenciat
Full swetly herd he confessio
ıı̄
un
And plesaunt was his absolucio
ıı̄
un
He was an esi man to yiue penaunce
There as he wist to haue a good petaunce
For vnto a poore ordre for to yiue
Is a signe that a man is well Ishriue
And if he yaf he durst make avaunt
He wist that a man was repentaunt
For many a man so harde is of his herte
He may nat wepe al thouȝ he sore smerte
Therfore in stede of weping and praiers
Men mot yeue siluer vnto poore freris
And certainli pinnes for to yiue faire wyfes
His tipet was ay farsed full of knifes
And certainli he had a mery note
Wel coude he synge and pleyen on the rote
Of tidinges he bar vtterli the pris
His necke white as any flour delys
Therto as strong was as any champio
ıı̄
un
He knew the tauernes wel in eueri toun̄
And eueri hosteler and tapstere
Rather than a beggere or a Lazer
For vnto such a worthi man as he
Accordeth nat as be his faculte
To haue with such Lazers aqueintaunce
It is nat honest it may nat avaunce
For to dele with no such poraill
But alle with riche and sellers of vitaill
And ouer all ther as proufit shuld arise
Curteis he was and louli of seruice
Ther was noman nowher so vertuous
He was the best begger in his hous
And yaf a certain ferme for the graunt
Non of his bretheren cam there in his haunt
For thouȝ a widewe had but a shoo
So plesant was his In principio
Yet wolde he haue a ferthing or he went
His purchas was welbetter than his rent
And rage he coude as it were a whelpe
In Louedayes coude he mochel helpe
For he ne was like no cloistrer
With thredebare cope as is a poore scoler
But he was like a maister or a Pope
Of double worsted was his semy cope
That round as was a belle out of a presse
Somwhat he lipsed for his wantounesse
To make his englissh swete vpon his tonge
And in harping whan that he had songe
His yhen twinkeled in his hed ariȝt
As don theȝ sterres in the frosty niȝt
This Lymytour was I cleped Huberd
A
Marchaunt ther was with a forked berd
In motley and high on hors he sat
Vpon his hed a flaundrissh beuer hatt
His bootes clapsed faire and fetisly
His resons he spak ful solemply
Shewing alwey thencres of his winning
He wold the see were kept for any thing
Betwix Middilbourgh and Orwell
He coude wel in eschaunging sheldes selle
This worthi man full wel his witt beset
Ther wist no wiȝt that he was in dette
So estatli was he in his gouernaunce
With his bargeins and his cheuesshaunce
For sothe he was a worthi man with all
But soth to sein I nat what men him call
A
clerk ther was of Oxenford also
That vnto Logiq
ue
longe had goo
And lene was his hors as is a rake
And he was nat riȝt fat I vndertake
But loked all lowe and therto sobirly
Ful thredebare was his ouerest courtby
For he gete him no benefice
Ne he was worldli to haue an office
For him were leuer at his beddes hed
Twenti bookes clad in white and red
Of Aristotle and of his Philosophie
Than Roberich or Fedill or Sawtrie
But al be it he was a Philosophre
Yet had he but litil gold in cofre
But al that he miȝt of his frendes hente
On bookes and on lerning he it spente
And besili gan for the soules preie
For hem of whom he had his scoley
Of studie took he most cure and hede
Nouȝt oo word spake he more than was nede
And that was seide in forme of reuerence
And short and quik and full of sentence
Souning in moral vertu was his speche
And gladli wold he lerne
and
gladli teche
A
Sergeaunt of Lawe was there wise
That often had ben at Paruys
He was also full riche of excellence
Discrete he was and of gret reuerence
He semed such his wordes were so wise
Iustice he was fuloften in assise
By patent and be plein co
m
missio
ıı̄
un
Of fees and robes he had many on̄
So gret a purchasour nowher was non̄
All was fee simple to him in effecte
His purchasing miȝt nat be infect
Noman̄ so besi a man̄ ther nas
And yit he semed besier than he was
In termes had he his cas
and
domes alle
That fro the tyme of king william were falle
Therto he coude endite and make a thing
Ther coude no wiȝt pinche at his enditing
And eueri statute coude he pleinli be rote
He rod but homly in a medled cote
I girt with a seint of silk with barres smale
Of his array telle I no lenger tale
A
Franklein was in his companie
White was his berde as is the daisie
Of his complexion he was sanguein
Wel loued he in the morwen a sop in wyne
To lyuen in delit was euer his wone
For he was Epicurious ougne sone
That hield opinio
ıı̄
un
that plein delite
Was verri felicite parfit
An housholder and that a gret was he
Seint Iulian he was in his contre
His bred his Ale was alwey aftir oon̄
A better envined man was ther non
Withoute bake mete was neuer his hous
Of fissh and flessh that was so plentevous
It souned in his hous of mete
and
drinke
Of all deintees that men coude bethink
Aftir the sondri seasons of the yere
So chaungeth he his mete
and
his souper
Full many a fat Pertrich had he in his mewe
And many a breme
and
many a luce in stewe
Woo was his cook but if his sauce were
Poynant and sharp and redi all his gere
His table dormant in his halle alwey
Stood redi couered all the long day
At Sessions there was he lord and sire
Oft tyme he was kniȝt of the shire
An Anlas and a gipser all of silk
Heng at his girdill as white as morne milk
A Sheriff had he be and Countour
Was nat where such anothir Vauasour
A
N haberdassher and a Carpenter
A webster a dyer and a Tapecer
And thei were clothed all in a lyuere
Of a solempne and agret fraternite
Full fressh and newe her gere piked was
Her knyues chaped nouȝt was with bras
But wrouȝt with siluer all full shene
and
well
Her girdeles and her pouches eueri dell
Wel semed ech of hem a faire burgeis
To sitten in a yelde halle vpon̄ a deys
Eueri forth wisdam that he can
Was lich shape to ben an Alderman̄
For catell had they Inouȝ and rente
And eke her wifes wold it well assente
And elles certein they be to blame
Hit is full faire to be cleped madame
And go to vigilies all before
And haue amantell roiallich I bore
A cook they had with hem for the nones
To boyle the chekenes with the mary bones
And pouder tart marchaunt
and
ganyngale
Wel coude he knowe a drauȝt of London Ale
He coude roste and sethe and boile and frye
Make mortrewes and wel bake a Pye
But gret was it as thouȝt me
That on his shine a mormall had he
For Blanmanger made with the beste
A
shipman̄ was ther woning fer be west
For ouȝt I wot he was of Dertmouthe
He rod vpon a Rounce as he couthe
In a goune of falding to the kne
A dagger hanging on a lace had he
Aboute his necke vnder his arme adoun̄
The hoot somer had made his hewe al broun̄
And certainli he was a good felawe
Full many a drauȝt of wyn had he drawe
From Burdeuxward whil the Marchant slepe
Of nice conscience took he no kepe
If he faught and had the higher hand
Be water he sent hem hom from eueri lond
But of his craft to rekne wel his tithes
The stremes and the daungers him besithes
His herbergh and monee Lodemanage
Ther was non̄ such from hull to Cartage
He hardi was and wyse I vndertake
With many atempest hath his berd be shake
He knewe well al the hauenes as they were
From Scotland vnto Capefenestere
And eueri crikke in Britayne and in Spaine
His barge it was I cleped the Magdeleine
U
ith vs ther was a doctour of Phisiq
ue
In all the world ther was non lik
To speken of Phisiq
ue
and Surgerie
For he was grounded in Astronomie
He kept his pacience a full gret dell
In houres be his making naturell
Wel coude he forme the ascendent
Of his ymage for his pacient
He knewe the cause of eueri maladie
Were it colde hoot moist or drie
And where it engendreth and of what humo
ᵘ
ur
He was a verri parfit Practisour
The cause he knewe of eueri harme the rote
Anon he yaf the seke man his bote
For redi had he his appotecaries
To sende him drugges and lectuaries
For ich of hem made othir to winne
Her frendship was nat newe to beginne
Wel knewe he the olde Esculapius
And Diascorides and eke Ruphus
Olde Ipocras Haly and Galien
Serapis Rasy and Apien
Bernard Gatisden and Gilbertine
Auerois Damassien and Constantine
Of his diete mesurable was he
For it was of no superfluite
But gret norisshing and digestible
His study nas but litil on the bible
In sanguein
and
Perse I clad was he all
I lyned with tiffata and with Sendall
And yit he nas but esi of his dispence
He kepte that he wan in pestilence
For gold in Phisiq
ue
is accordiall
Therfor he loued gold in especiall
A
good wif ther was beside Bathe
But she was somdel deth
and
that was scathe
Of cloth making she had such an haunt
She passed hem of Pris and of Gaunt
In all the parissh wif was ther non
That to the offring beforn hir shuld gon
And if ther did certein so wroth was she
That she was out of all charite
Her kirchis full fyne were of ground
I durst well sweren they weyeden x pound
That on the sonday were vpon hir hed
Her hosen were of fyn scarlet red
Ful streite I teyed and shoes ful moist
and
newe
Bold was hir face
and
faire and red of hewe
She was a worthi womman̄ al her lif
Husbondes at the chirche dore had she fyue
Beside othir companie in youthe
For therof nede nouȝt to speke of nouthe
And thries had she ben at Iherusalem
She hath passed many a straunge strem
At Rome had she been and at Boleyn̄
In Caleis at Seint Iames and at Coleyn̄
She couthe moch of wandring be the weye
Gat tothed was she sotheli for to seie
Vpon an ambler esily she satt
I wympled and on hir hed an hatt
As brod as it were a bokeler or a targe
A foot mantell aboute hir hipes large
And on hir heles a peire of spores sharpe
In felauship coude she wel laughe
and
carpe
Of remedies of loue she knew
ꝑ
par
chaunce
For she knewe of that art the diliaunce
A
good man was there of religio
ıı̄
un
And was a poore Person of a toun̄
But riche he was of holi thouȝt and werk
He was also a lerned man̄ a clerk
That cristes gospell wold preche and teche
His
ꝑ
par
isshons deuoutly wold he teche
Benigne he was and wonder diligent
And in such aduersite full pacient
And such he was proued ofte sithes
Full loth were him to cursen for his tithes
But rather wold he yiue hem out of doute
Vnto his poore parisshons aboute
Of his offring and his substaunce
He couthe in litill thing haue suffisaunce
Wide was his parissh and houses fer asonder
But he ne left nouȝt for no reyne ne thonder
In sekenes or in mischef to visite
The forthest in his parissh moch
and
lite
Vpon̄ his feet and in his hand a staf
This noble ensample vnto his shepe he yaf
That first he wrouȝt
and
aftirward he tauȝt
And in the gospell tho wordes he rauȝt
And this figure eke he added therto
That if gold ruste what shuld Iren doo
For if a preest be a fooll on whom we truste
No wonder is a leude man to ruste
And shame it is if a preest take kepe
A shetin shepperd and a clene shepe
Well ouȝte a preest ensample for to yeue
Be his clennesse hou his shepe shuld lyue
He set nouȝt the benefice to hire
And left his shepe acombred in the myre
And renne to Londo
ıı̄
un
vnto seint Poules
To take him a Chauntrie for soules
Othir with a Brotherhod to be witholde
But duelt at hom and kepte wel his folde
So that the wolf may it nouȝt miscarye
He was a Shepperd and nat a mercenarie
And thouȝ he holi were and vertuous
He nas nat to sinfull despitous
Ne of his shepe daungerous and digne
But in teching discret and benigne
To drawe folk to heuene be fairnesse
Be good ensample this was his besinesse
But yef it were any persone obstinat
Whedir he were high or lowe estat
Him wold snibben̄ sharpeli for the nones
A better preste I trowe nowher non is
He wayted aftir no pompe ne reuerence
Ne makid him a spiced conscience
Of cristes lore and his aposteles twelue
He tauȝt but first he folwed it him selue
U
ith him ther was a plouȝ man̄ his brother
That had I led of donge full many afother
A trewe swinker and a good was he
Leuing in pees and in parfit chastite
God loued he best with all his herte
At all tymes were it game or smerte
And than his neiȝbour right as himself
He wold thressh and therto dike and delue
For cristes sake with eueri pouer wiȝt
Withoute hyre yef it lay in his miȝt
His tithes paid he full faire and well
Bothe of his propre swinke
and
his catell
In a tabard he rod vpon a mere
T
her was also a Reue a Mellere
A Sompnor and a Pardoner also
A Manciple and my self and namo
The Millere was a stoute carll for the nones
Full big he was of braun̄ and bones
That proued wel for ouerall ther he cam
At the wrasteling he wold ay haue the Ram
He was short shuldred thikke squarre
Ther was no dore that he ne wold heue of þᵉ harre
Or breke it at arenne with his hed
His berd as any cole fox was red
And therto brode as any spade
Vpon̄ his coppe of his nose a wrette he hade
And theron̄ stood a tuft of heres
Red as the bristelis of sowes eres
His nose thrilles blake were and wide
A swerd and a bokeler bar he be his side
His mouth as gret was as a forneys
He was a iangeler and a galiardeys
And that was most of synne and harlotries
Wel coude he stele corn and tolle thries
And yit had he a thombe of gold parde
A white cote and a blew hood had he
A bag pipe wel coude he blowe
and
soune
And therwith all he brouȝt vs out of toune
A
gentil Manciple ther was of a temple
